definitions.explanation: In anthropology, the earliest stage of human ancestors, such as the australopithecines, regarded as a link between apes and humans. The oldest of the textbook stages {猿人|えんじん} → {原人|げんじん} → {旧人|きゅうじん} → {新人|しんじん}.

examples.japanese: {猿人|えんじん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{化石|かせき}→化石：11796_kaseki⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}つかった→見つかる：01173_mitsukaru⟧。
examples.english: Fossils of an early hominid were found.

examples.japanese: {猿人|えんじん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{二足歩行|にそくほこう}→二足歩行：29490_nisokuhokou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦していた→する：00392_suru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{考|かんが}えられている→考える：00856_kangaeru⟧。
examples.english: Australopithecines are thought to have walked on two legs.

examples.japanese: ⟦{人類|じんるい}→人類：01578_jinrui⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{進化|しんか}→進化：06029_shinka⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{猿人|えんじん}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{原人|げんじん}→原人：29467_genjin⟧⟦へ→へ：02473_he⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{段階的|だんかいてき}→段階的：06174_dankaiteki⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{進|すす}んだ→進む：01225_susumu⟧。
examples.english: Human evolution proceeded in stages from ape-men to early humans.

notes:
A technical term in physical anthropology for the earliest grade of human ancestor.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {猿人|えんじん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{化石|かせき}→化石：11796_kaseki⟧: hominid fossils
- ⟦{初期|しょき}→初期：11742_shoki⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{猿人|えんじん}: early hominids
- {猿人|えんじん}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{進化|しんか}→進化：06029_shinka⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to evolve from ape-men

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{原人|げんじん}→原人：29467_genjin⟧: Homo erectus stage — the next grade after {猿人|えんじん}
- ⟦{類人猿|るいじんえん}→類人猿：18454_ruijinen⟧: great ape — living apes such as the gorilla and chimpanzee, not human ancestors
